newsitem.title: USA: Key IMM currencies end up after quiet afternoon.
newsitem.headline: Key IMM currencies end up after quiet afternoon.

text.p: Key IMM currency futures finished higher and near the middle of the day's range after a quiet afternoon.
June marks, Swiss francs and yen ended slightly higher but below early highs. Canadian dollar and Sterling ended lower.

Players took to the sidelines before the weekend and after recent rallies in yen and Canadian dollar, traders said. Canada's markets will be shut Monday in observance of Victoria Day, and markets will be fixated on Tuesday's U.S. Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) meeting, traders said.
"It's the end of the week, the beginning of FOMC and no dollar comments, so we were just stuck there," an IMM futures trader said.

Traders said the day's data did little to clear up uncertainty about what the Fed's policy arm will do when it meets Tuesday. Some traders said participants were evenly divided between the Fed standing pat and raising rates 25 basis points. Others said the week's data as a whole shaves the likelihood of a rate hike to just below 50 percent.
Ideas that interest rate differentials between the U.S. and Japan has been a key driver of the recent yen rally.

Morning trade was heavy, with action dominated by yen as it challenged resistance levels on the heels of strong gains Thursday. Bouts of profit taking kept the market choppy, traders noted, but added the yen uptrend is intact.

Early in the session, U.S. April housing starts rose 2.6 percent to a 1.473 million annual rate. Market sources reported the University of Michigan consumer sentiment index rose to a record high 104.6.
June Canadian dollar soared to a two-month high early on bullish fundamental momentum from Thursday, but cut its gains near midday.
"We saw profit taking late in the day in Canada, but nothing has really changed," a trading floor source said. "It was technically driven in a nervous market," he said.

At the close, June yen was up $0.000015 at $0.008680, marks rose $0.0016 to $0.5921, Swiss francs rose $0.0042 to $0.7061, sterling was off $0.0074 at $1.6360, Can dollar fell $0.0008 to $0.7293, Aus dollar fell $0.0025 to $0.7751, Mex peso was up $0.000025 at $0.125150.
